title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is developing a 'surgery' theory for conformal surfaces (Riemann surfaces, possibly with boundary). The basic operation is to cut a surface along a closed set K and glue it back along boundary homeomorphisms σ, then ask whether the result carries a conformal structure extending the given one. On the previous page, 'Lemme 3' reduces the general gluing statement to two local model cases.

Case a) (previous page). Glue the half-disc H = {z : |z|<1, Im z ≥ 0} to itself (or to a copy) along a 'rectifiable' homeomorphism σ:[0,1]→[0,1] that is regular near 0. A variant uses [-1,1]→[-1,1].

Case b) (this page). Glue the closed half-disc H̄ to itself along a rectifiable involution σ that exchanges [0,1] and [-1,0], with σ(0)=0, regular near 0. This is the local model of a 'folding' or 'zipping' point. If σ(x) = -x, the result near 0 is a sector of angle π with its two edges identified. That is a cone of total angle π, made conformally regular by z ↦ z². So 0 becomes an interior point of the glued surface. The lemma asserts that the glued space inherits a conformal structure. In modern terms this is a local conformal-welding statement.

Margin (12.1 c), partly illegible). Begins a further case: C an analytic curve in a conformal surface X, interior, with a neighbourhood U.

Section (4), 'Recollements des disques'. The edge-to-edge gluings are covered by Theorem 4 in the case where K is a compact 1-manifold and S = ∅. To get more manageable cases, Grothendieck imposes natural restrictive conditions on the involution σ of ∂X̃. Key recollection: let X be a conformal surface with boundary and C a boundary component. Then two data are equivalent:
- a (rectifiable) structure of real projective line on C, i.e. an identification C ≅ RP¹ up to PGL(2,R);
- a 'bouchage de trou', i.e. capping the hole C by a disc D to get X' = X ∪_C D.
Given a cap, uniformize D ≅ unit disc. The boundary values identify C with ∂D = RP¹, well defined up to Aut(D) = PSL(2,R), which acts projectively on the circle. Conversely, a projective identification is used to weld in a standard disc. Regularity of the projective structure (e.g. compatibility with the real-analytic structure of C) mirrors the regularity of C as a curve in X'.

Next page continues this. Choosing a centre a ∈ D amounts to reducing the structure group PGL(2,R) to its maximal compact PO(2) = O(2)/±1, since D is the hyperbolic plane PGL(2,R)/PO(2). Equivalently, it gives a 'linear' (circle) structure on ∂D = C, and a canonical embedding D ⊂ T_{X',a}. Grothendieck is heading toward a Proposition stating an equivalence of categories. In modern language: {cappings of a boundary circle} ≈ {homeomorphisms C → RP¹ of a suitable regularity}/PSL(2,R), and {centred cappings} ≈ the same modulo the rotation group S¹.
errors: The equivalence 'projective-line structure on C ⇔ capping by a disc' is only correct under welding hypotheses. For an arbitrary homeomorphism C → RP¹ the conformal welding may fail to exist. Even when it exists it may be non-unique if the resulting curve is not conformally removable. Quasisymmetric maps (relative to the analytic structure of C) give existence and uniqueness (Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen). Grothendieck's undefined qualifier 'rectifiable' is presumably meant to handle this but is not specified on this page.

'Structure de droite projective' must be understood globally: an identification of C with RP¹, developing map a homeomorphism of degree 1. A merely locally projective structure on the circle can have nontrivial holonomy or winding and does not give a disc capping.
In case b) the transcription reads 'respectant au voisinage du pt 0'. The intended condition is presumably regularity of σ near 0, as in case a).

ideas.what: Gluing a half-disc to itself along a folding involution of the diameter (σ(0)=0) as a local model in the existence of conformal structures after surgery
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (welding theorem); zipper ideas by Marshall, Rohde and others later

ideas.what: Capping a boundary circle of a bordered Riemann surface by a disc is equivalent to giving a real projective-line structure on that circle, with regularity of one mirroring regularity of the other
ideas.modern_name: conformal welding correspondence; Diff(S¹)/PSL(2,R) ↔ cappings (universal Teichmüller space / Segal-type sewing data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conformal welding: Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen. As a moduli-theoretic principle: Kirillov (1987), Segal (CFT definition, 1987–88), Nag–Verjovsky

ideas.what: Choosing a centre of the capping disc equals reducing the structure group PGL(2,R) of the projective line C to PO(2), with canonical embedding D ⊂ T_{X',a} (next page)
ideas.modern_name: hyperbolic disc as PGL(2,R)/PO(2); cappings with marked centre ↔ Diff(S¹)/S¹ (Kirillov's univalent-function model); local coordinates at a puncture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kirillov (1987), Kirillov–Yuriev; Segal; Vafa / Friedan–Shenker style moduli of punctured surfaces with local coordinates

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck sets up conformal surgery with an explicit dictionary. Boundary-circle cappings correspond to projective structures on the circle; centred cappings correspond to the reduction PGL(2,R) → PO(2). This is essentially the picture behind Segal's sewing axioms for CFT and Kirillov's identification of Diff(S¹)/S¹ (and Diff(S¹)/PSL(2,R)) with spaces of conformal weldings and univalent functions. Both appeared in 1987, independently and slightly later. Grothendieck's framing as an equivalence of categories, and as a tool to classify edge-to-edge gluings via restrictions on the involution σ, appears to be unrecorded.
missed.quote: il revient au même de se donner une structure de droite projective sur C, ou un "bouchage de trou" en C par un disque
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an early, independent formulation of the 'surfaces with parametrized boundary and sewing' formalism, motivated by dessins / Teichmüller-tower considerations rather than physics. This is of historical interest for the genesis of the Esquisse d'un programme surgery viewpoint.

missed.claim: The programme of finding 'natural restrictive conditions' on the boundary involution σ so that edge-to-edge gluings always yield conformal surfaces (via 'rectifiable' homeomorphisms) is left open. The modern answer would use quasisymmetric or Weil–Petersson-class homeomorphisms and conformal removability.
missed.quote: il est naturel de dégager des conditions restrictives naturelles sur l'involution σ sur ∂X̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly superseded by welding theory. It only matters as a record of how Grothendieck intended to make surgery rigorous.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical conformal welding, stated without the necessary hypotheses. The interest is historical: an explicit 1983–84 dictionary of cappings ↔ projective structures on circles and centres ↔ PO(2)-reductions, anticipating the Segal/Kirillov formalism, in an unpublished surgery programme.
transcription_corrections: 'bordage de trou' should read 'bouchage de trou' (consistent with 'bouchage des trous' on the next page).
'dans le cas 4' is more likely 'dans le Th. 4'.
'(... lien de X̃)' is likely '(au lieu de X̃)'.
'(cf. ...: la structure analytique réelle de C)' is probably 'Cf. ex.: la structure analytique réelle de C'.
In line 3, 'respectant au voisinage du pt 0' is uncertain; by analogy with case a) the intended condition is probably regularity near 0.
Margin note: '12.1 [b)] c) Soit C une courbe analytique ... dans une surface conforme X ...' — the rest is mostly illegible; 'Hol_φ' is doubtful.
